title: HS Prannoy, Anmol Kharb Progress to Taipei Open Second Round
indian_angle: Top Indian shuttler HS Prannoy and rising star Anmol Kharb both secured wins, advancing to the next stage of an international tournament.
summary: HS Prannoy secured a dominant opening-round victory in 35 minutes, while Anmol Kharb also successfully progressed to the second round of the Taipei Open 2026.

title: PV Sindhu Clinches Japan Open Crown with Dominant Win Over Akane Yamaguchi
indian_angle: India's star shuttler PV Sindhu ended her title drought by securing a major international Super 750 title, defeating a strong home contender.
summary: PV Sindhu delivered a scorching performance to win the Japan Open title, overcoming home favorite Akane Yamaguchi in the final and ending a period of doubt about her form.

title: BAI Releases Eligibility Criteria for World Junior Championships 2026 Selection
indian_angle: The circular outlines the specific requirements for Indian junior players aspiring to represent the nation at the prestigious BWF World Junior Championships in Cairo.
summary: The Badminton Association of India has issued a circular detailing the player eligibility criteria for selection to the BWF World Junior Championships 2026, scheduled to be held in Cairo, Egypt.

title: Delhi Prepares to Host BWF World Championships 2026, Focus on New Fans
indian_angle: India will host the prestigious BWF World Championships in Delhi, with discussions focusing on attracting a new generation of fans to the sport.
summary: As Delhi gears up to host the BWF World Championships 2026, there's a strong emphasis on engaging Gen Z and Gen Alpha audiences to broaden badminton's appeal in India.

title: BAI Adopts 3x15 Scoring System for Domestic Junior Tournaments
indian_angle: This significant rule change will impact all U-13, U-15, and U-17 domestic ranking tournaments and national championships across India.
summary: The Badminton Association of India has announced the implementation of a new 3x15 scoring system for all domestic ranking tournaments and national championships in the U-13, U-15, and U-17 age categories, starting at Ernakulam.

title: BAI President Sarma Comments on Monkeys at India Open: 'What is the problem?'
indian_angle: The head of the Badminton Association of India, Himanta Biswa Sarma, offered a unique perspective on the presence of monkeys during a major tournament in India.
summary: BAI President Himanta Biswa Sarma made a notable comment regarding the presence of monkeys during the India Open, questioning why it would be considered a problem for them to watch a game.
